Hi @Blad3forc3 , you can mount the iso into the rom folder and it should work out of the box.

Option 1: You can use fuse iso, install it with:

```
sudo apt-get install fuseiso # for debian-based
sudo pacman -S fuseiso # for arch-base
```

And use it as `fuseiso ~/Downloads/my-game.iso my-game/rom`. To unmount use `fusermount -u my-game/rom`.

Option 2: You can use the mount command (requires superuser):

To mount use: `sudo mount -o loop ~/Downloads/my-game.iso my-game/rom`, and to unmount use `sudo umount my-game/rom`.

I use cd emu to mount my images:

cdemu load 0 *path to cd image* my-game/rom

I was completely overthinking it.
enable wine-mono
winetricks cmd
winetricks vcrun2015
winetricks xact_x64

dump the contents of skse64.7z into skyrim root directory
same for mo2.7s (don't use a folder, use skyrim install directory as mo2 portable root directory)

test skyrim launcher, set your default graphics options, boot into wagon scene, create inis
test mo2 launcher.exe
use global instance
create and set all directories except base dir and profiles directory to a folder in c:\users\user\documents\my games\Skyrim Special Edition GOG
create and set profile directory to c:\users\user\appdata\local
done here

will throw an error and use "microsoft" profile by default. this is fine.
change active profile to Skyrim Special Edition GOG (This must always be your profile. MO2 just doesn't like using gog's proper folder to write loadorder files to even on windows- this is a workaround)
close mo2
quit gameimage
restart gameimage, do not overwrite anything, just continue up to where you were before
build and test. ./AppRun won't work before you build the appimage itself, but it should once you're done.
If you're using a steam version, or if/when mo2 ever fixes the profiles issue, that step should in theory follow the same steps as the other mo2 paths
When you run it under a username under the one you created it under, you're gotta reset the paths in mo2 and copy the files over from the hidden directory next to the appimage

This checks if the host has `cdemu` installed, if it is, use it. Otherwise, it uses the `AppImage`.

```sh
if command -v cdemu &>/dev/null; then
  notify-send "Using host-provided cdemu..."

I managed to make it work as a portable AppImage with an external prefix

* Export the package type as `prefix`
    ```
    export GIMG_PKG_TYPE=prefix
    ```
* Start with a fresh prefix (erase build/AppDir/app/wine or the entire build directory)
* Fetch tools
* Run configure phase to initialize the wine prefix
* Select win32
* Do not install dxvk nor vkd3d
* Run wine winecfg and select windows98 compatibility mode
* Type continue to finish the configure phase
* Exit the program with `continue` or with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>  + <kbd>D</kbd>
* Copy the install folder to inside build/AppDir/app/wine/drive_c
* Export the install folder location as an extra rom dir, inside `drive_c`
    ```
    # Execute this command in the same folder as the rom and icon folders
    export GIMG_DIR_ROM_EXTRA="\"$(pwd)/build/AppDir/app/wine/drive_c/tourcar\""
    ```
* Re-execute gameimage and open the install phase
* Install the game from inside the `drive_c` path, `drive_c/tourcar/setup.exe`
* Drop the dgvoodoo2 `D3DImm.dll` and `DDraw.dll` on the installed folder, `drive_c/Codemast/TourCar/`
* Re-execute the configure phase and run `wine winecfg`
* Add the native overrides for `d3dimm` and `ddraw` in winecfg
* Build and use `drive_c/Codemast/TourCar/setup.exe` and the default `.exe`

That should do it, however now you have to backup both the appimage and the prefix. It should work with other package methods besides `prefix`, but my guess is that it does not due to [this](https://gitlab.com/formigoni/gameimage/-/issues/21) issue.

Hi @casasfernando , thanks for checking out the project!

> I would really prefer read-only AppImages, so I can sync them once to my gaming PC and my Steam Deck, but then I only have to sync the overlayfs data with the saved games, instead of the whole app package again (which can be several GBs).

Not sure if I understood correctly, but for flatimage, you only require to sync the .my-game.flatimage.config directory, which will contain your saves & other data. Same as it would be for AppImage.

> Would the AppImage method continue to be maintained moving forward or only FlatImage?

AppImage will be completely dropped in the next version, it does not allow the project to achieve its portability goal.

> Would it be possible to have the best of both packages and have read-only FlatImages (still using overlayfs for changing data like saved games, etc)?

Flatimage is not read-only, but game data is already stored in the overlayfs directory. So from what I understood it already does what you expect.

> One thing I noticed is that while the AppImage is running in the .config directory that is created in the same directory as the AppImage there is a directory called wine that is taking a lot of disk space (3GB in my case) and that is cleaned up when the AppImage stops running. Is this necessary?

The image is mounted to /tmp, and the overlayfs mountpoint is set to the .my-game.AppImage.config/wine directory, this allows the changes that are made by the game (creating and modifying save data) to persist in .my-game.AppImage.config/union after the game is closed. The mountpoint was chosen to be in this configuration directory because some applications do not allow running under /tmp.

Edit: It does not get cleared up, it gets un-mounted. So this 3GB of space you're seeing is not copied on startup.

Ah I see, at this time flatimage does not support read-only execution. The flatimage file contains the mutable filesystem that is mounted to `/tmp/fim/instance/...`, it is mounted as r/w, so that is probably why r+x resulted in a failure. Even with the launcher disabled, without proper handling it will fail. For example, these are the mountpoints used when running `amnesia-a-machine-for-pigs`:
```
/tmp/fim/instance/71cf41a_20240323223540/mount/BOoBDm.mount.dwarfs.amnesia-a-machine-for-pigs
/tmp/fim/instance/71cf41a_20240323223540/mount/BOoBDm.mount.dwarfs.opt
/tmp/fim/instance/71cf41a_20240323223540/mount/BOoBDm.mount.dwarfs.usr
/tmp/fim/instance/71cf41a_20240323223540/mount/BOoBDm.mount.overlayfs.amnesia-a-machine-for-pigs
/tmp/fim/instance/71cf41a_20240323223540/mount/BOoBDm.mount.overlayfs.usr
```
Symlinks for these mountpoints are created inside the flatimage, which requires it to be writteable, the mount points cannot be created directly inside the mutable filesystem because fuse does not allow it by default.

I think the choice of QT or GTK would not be ideal, mainly because it would not be able to keep up to date for long. Iced seems to be pretty new, the documentation for is not as good as fltk's, but it does look pretty good. I use fltk-rs with a fixed look to be consistent and independent of what the host has. About C++ & rust, I do prefer C++, however I see this as a positive thing since many people find it difficult to use C++ and prefer rust, or already know C++ and do not see rust as something advantageous. No problem. It would not be that simple because the games are stored in compressed filesystems inside flatimage. The flatimage method of doing things does not require to extract everything to modify like it was with AppImage. Here are some examples, (make a backup before trying):

List the filesystems inside the image
```
$ ./tomb-raider-collection.flatimage fim-dwarfs-list
tomb-raider-anniversary
tomb-raider-legend
tomb-raider-underworld
usr
wine
```

Extract a game from the flatimage to the current directory (from the previous list):
```
./tomb-raider-collection.flatimage fim-exec cp /fim/dwarfs/tomb-raider-anniversary.dwarfs .
```

Extract a dwarfs file to a folder:
```
mkdir tomb-raider-anniversary
tomb-raider-collection.flatimage fim-exec dwarfsextract -i tomb-raider-anniversary.dwarfs -o tomb-raider-anniversary
```

Move the `tomb-raider-anniversary` directory and the `tomb-raider-anniversary.dwarfs` filesystem to the build directory of gameimage. On the creator, create click on '+', for adding a new game, type the same name of the directory/dwarfs file `tomb-raider-anniversary` and it should detect the folder and executables inside, without having to reinstall.


---

Update wine, with a new version downloaded from the [gameimage-runners](https://github.com/gameimage/runners/releases/tag/wine-gnu-x86_64) github. The name of the filesystem should be `wine.dwarfs`, the last argument is the mountpoint, games look for wine in this location.
```
./tomb-raider-collection.flatimage fim-dwarfs-add wine.dwarfs /fim/mount/wine
```

---

Note that I have not exposed this features yet because it is a bit experimental, if it is working I recommend to just leave it.

In the meantime, (while it's not a perfectly comparable experience) here is a somewhat functional workaround (though it would still require you to have the physical disk in a physical drive).
1. Take the iso of your game you are wanting to play (extracted via K3b, ImgBurn, etc.) and unpack it via an application such as "PeaZip".
2. When you reach the part of the gui process where you are asked to install the media, figure out how to do this for the files you have. For me, the extracted game files had a "setup.exe", which I selected, and I was prompted through the installation process for the game.
3. Once you reach the part of the GI gui process where you are prompted to select an executable for your FlatImage, insert your game disk into your physical drive and wait for it to mount.
4. Now, with your file-browser, go into the flatimage temporary "build" directory > "game_name" directory > "wine" directory > "dosdevices" directory.
5. Here, open your terminal and and use the following command: `ln -s "/path/to/your/currently/mounted/game/disk/directory/" "<lowercase_arbitrary_drive_letter_not_being_used>:"`. For me, I used the following: `ln -s "/media/me/Deer Hunter 2003/" "y:"`
6. After making the symbolic link, proceed with the GI gui process by selecting the executable you want the flatimage to use, etc.

By following this process, you should be able to launch your new flatimage game as long as the disk is in your physical drive.

With all of that said, I actually checked out CDEmu as well (while trying to find a convenient way to get my game portably working), and the above method, again, is certainly no replacement for CDEmu's functionality (assuming I understand the program's functionality correctly). No problem, I'm glad it worked out! You can drop the script in the same directory as the ones from the game to execute it. It hightly depends on what the script is doing, you will be running the script from inside a container, so things you install in the host won't be directly accessible. If want to use gamescope, you could experiment with something like:
```bash
# Set width and height to a default or use pre-existing values for `GAMESCOPEW` and `GAMESCOPEH`.
width=${GAMESCOPEW:-1920}
height=${GAMESCOPEH:-1080}
# Use gamescope if it is installed in the host
if command -v gamescope; then
    fim_portal gamescope -w $width -h $height -- /path/to/game/executable
else
  /path/to/game/executable
fi
```
`fim_portal` uses the `gamescope` from the host to run the game in the container. More details about `fim_portal` [here](https://flatimage.github.io/docs/portal/).

If the command is `./launch_openmohaa_base.x86_64 +set r_customwidth 3440 +set r_customheight 1440 +set r_mode -1` then it may not be executing `launch_openmohaa_base.x86_64` because it is on another working directory. Try this:

```sh
#!/bin/bash

DIR_SCRIPT="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

"$DIR_SCRIPT"/launch_openmohaa_base.x86_64 +set r_customwidth 3440 +set r_customheight 1440 +set r_mode -1
```

And make sure that the script in on the same directory as the `launch_openmohaa_base.x86_64` file.

Also remember to make the script and `launch_openmohaa_base.x86_64` executables with `chmod +x`.

Hello, you can run appimages inside a flatimage using the portal. For example, `fim_portal ./firefox.AppImage` would execute the appimage in the host. However, this is not recommended because running on the host requires dependencies that might not be available or the appimage itself might not run due to glibc issues (or if the system uses musl).

You could follow @Blackfox-Thane advice, but I would recommend extracting with `./App.AppImage --appimage-extract` and moving the `squashfs-root` directory to inside the flatimage with `./app.flatimage fim-exec cp ./squashfs-root /app`. This will copy the appimage application directory to `/app` and you can run with `./app.flatimage fim-exec /app/AppRun`. This will avoid extracting the app everytime you launch it.

Also @Blackfox-Thane, I think the command `fim-perms add "usr/lib" "/lib" ` is incorrect, since the list of valid permissions is:
```
home
media
wayland
xorg
dbus_user
network
````

I found a solution by using an open-source alternative to [steam-input](https://github.com/xan105/InputFusion), I'll integrate it in the GUI, but here's how to use it meanwhile:

- Install xinput in the wizard optional dependencies page (this automatically includes the wine overrides).
- Download the latest version of [InputFusion](https://github.com/xan105/InputFusion/releases).
- Determine which file to use from the `XInput` folder inside the zip file:
    - Do `file my-game.exe` to check if the binary of your game is 32-bit (i386) or 64-bit.
    - Do `strings my-game.exe | grep -i xinput` to check which version of xinput to use.
- Copy the correct file to the same directory `my-game.exe` is.

Now just check if the gamepad works properly by running the game.
